pieces.text: Years ago I was flipping channels, half-asleep, and landed in the middle of a movie I'd never seen. A man sat at a kitchen table, turning a coffee cup, saying nothing. I didn't know his name or what he'd done. I stayed standing forty minutes, remote in my fist, because the way that silence was held made me need to know what he'd do next. That is not luck. Somebody built the cup, the pause, the leaning-in. Before you inform anyone, or dazzle them, or polish a single line, you owe them a reason to lean toward your people in the dark. Get their heart clamped first. Everything clever you buried underneath only gets spent if they already ache to know what happens. Earn that, or nothing else you made will land.

On WALL·E I once wrote a beat that spelled out the little robot was lonely, so no one could miss it. We cut it. We just let him sort the day's collected junk onto his shelves at night, alone, and said nothing about what it meant. The room went quiet and leaned in. They built the loneliness themselves, out of a lamp and a boot and a robot who kept the pretty things. That is the trade. Hand people a finished answer and they nod and drift off. Leave the right thing unsaid, hold the gap open, and they lean in to close it — and whatever a person assembles with their own hands, they will not set down. Less, held well, is the hook.

When I was nine, a great-uncle sat me on the porch and began a story like this: 'The summer I turned twelve, I found a dead man in our well, and I never told a soul who put him there.' I did not move for an hour. I knew nothing about that summer yet, but the first breath of it swore to me that it was going somewhere, and that where it went would be worth the sitting. That is the whole job of an opening. Not to dazzle — to make a promise the reader can feel in the chest, an oath that this will pay. A reader forgives a slow stretch in the middle if page one gave its word. Break the promise and they close the book. Keep it, and that small vow is the thing that carries them, page after page, all the way to the last one.
